summary: Iteration 178 — Admin Analytics dashboard for SignGuy AI. Full backend (38 tests, all passing) and frontend testing. All 15 requirements verified.

issues: 'ANONYMOUS VI...' stat card label truncates — 'ANONYMOUS VISITS' is cut off on smaller widths. Minor cosmetic only (data is correct).

critical_code_review_comments: analytics.js trackEvent() uses fire-and-forget fetch — good design, no await blocking the app.
PageTracker fires on [location.pathname, user] — if user object changes (e.g. after profile refresh), it can re-fire a page_view for the same page. Low risk but worth noting.

initErrorTracking adds event listeners every time user?.id changes — if called multiple times with same user, duplicate listeners stack up (window.addEventListener doesn't dedupe). Could cause duplicate error events. Consider using removeEventListener or a 'initialized' flag guard.
analytics_users endpoint does N+1 queries (1 per user × 5 collections) — not an issue at 100 users but will need aggregation pipeline or caching at scale.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Admin Analytics feature is fully functional. All 8 API endpoints work correctly with proper RBAC (403 for non-platform_admin). Event ingestion (POST /api/analytics/event) is public, returns {ok: true}, correctly inserts to analytics_events. MongoDB indexes verified (all 6 required: timestamp, event_type, session_id, user_id, route, ip_address). No infinite loop — /api/analytics/event route is never stored as a tracked page_view. Page views firing correctly on navigation. All 8 tabs render correctly (Overview/Charts/Users have real data; Routes/Sessions/Referrers/Errors show expected empty states; Suspicious tab shows real bot traffic). Access control redirects non-admin to / with 'Access denied' toast. One minor code review note: initErrorTracking may stack duplicate window event listeners if called multiple times — add a guard flag.
rca_of_issues: No critical issues found. The only minor code quality concern is initErrorTracking() adding event listeners on user?.id change without deduplication — but this does NOT cause app crashes, only potential double-reporting of errors in edge cases.
